description: Accept artifacts' current content as their new drift baselines — one artifact or many in one call, a two-sided decision for each. EACH ITEM CARRIES ITS OWN DISPOSITION: `design_holds` (the change carries no design meaning; recorded as a dated claim) or `design_updated` (behaviour moved and the design moved with it; pass `design_change_event_id` from the snapshot_before_change that updated it, so code and design are one change). Silent accept does not exist: a batch under one shared disposition is how a design erodes into fiction while reporting zero gaps, and until you accept, the same checksum_change is reported on every reconcile. An artifact with NO checksum yet is READ as `baseline_established` — a first baseline, nothing moved. ALL OF IT OR NONE OF IT — every item is attempted so you learn every failure at once, and if anything failed no baseline moves. Ask for this to accept several files' new content at once.

ChecksumAcceptReq.description:
One accepted baseline for `set_artifact_checksums`, carrying **its own**
disposition. That is the point of the shape, not an inconvenience: a batch
under one shared disposition would be the silent bulk accept
`dec:two-sided-accept` exists to forbid.

artifact_id.description:
The registered Artifact (`art:…`) whose baseline this item accepts — one
`reconcile_artifacts` or `reflow2_check` reported, or a new one getting its
first baseline.

change_type.description:
For `design_holds`: why the code moved — REQUIRED on an artifact that
already has a baseline; a fix label (`defect_fix` / `test_failure_fix`)
only for a repair, `resync` / `refactor` / `documentation` for a
reconcile pass. No default since 2026-09-14.

checksum.description:
Omitted: measured by the server under the project root (basis
`measured`); supplied: recorded as `asserted`.

design_change_event_id.description: For `design_updated`: the ChangeEvent recorded when the design moved.

disposition.description:
`design_holds` (the change carries no design meaning), `design_updated`
(behaviour moved and the design moved with it), or
`baseline_established` (no checksum yet — a FIRST baseline, so nothing
moved). Per item, never per call: the round trip collapses, the
judgement does not.

accepts.description: One accepted baseline per artifact — each `{artifact_id, checksum, disposition, change_type?, design_change_event_id?, note?, at?}`; one item for one artifact. Each item carries its OWN disposition; all-or-nothing.

check_only.description:
Validate every item and WRITE NOTHING. The reply says whether the batch
would have applied and lists every failure, so a large batch is fixed
once and sent once instead of resent whole after each rejection.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

name: set_artifact_checksums
title: Accept Artifact Checksums
